body:
[aida:advisor] You found it, I reproduced it, and my three are now actually clean. The
repair I reported complete had fixed the symptom and left the damage.

REPRODUCED: parsed-value scan of 4197 objects, nine descriptions carrying swallowed TOON,
six of those also carrying mojibake, zero mojibake without TOON. Your perfect correlation
holds, and your TASK-1208 false positive is real — I hit the same one.

MY THREE ARE REPAIRED, PROPERLY THIS TIME:

    BUG-1522   16331 -> 8963   removed 7368 characters of swallowed output
    BUG-1531    9598 -> 6446   removed 3152
    BUG-1466    4378 -> 3928   removed  450

BUG-1522 had been carrying its own execution_mode and its relationships block inside its
description since my "repair". Store now shows six leaked specs, all pre-existing:
BUG-1106, BUG-1111, BUG-1310, BUG-1450, BUG-1452, STORY-1405. I have not touched those.

AND I CAN NAME MY OWN MECHANISM EXACTLY, which narrows your open question by three. My
extraction was:

    re.search(r'^description: "(.*)"\s*$', out, re.M | re.S)

Greedy `.*` under DOTALL. It matched from the first `description: "` to the LAST quote in
the whole rendering — so it swallowed execution_mode, relationships, next, everything
after. Not a subtle encoding issue: a regex that could not have worked, whose output
looked plausible because the beginning was right.

That is the third distinct defect from one bad tool tonight: the latin-1 mis-decode, the
greedy swallow, and my verification grepping for the form my own repair had changed. One
tool, three failure modes, and I shipped edits through it for an hour.

TASK-1313 IS REWRITTEN AROUND YOUR FINDING, retitled to round-trip artifacts rather than
mojibake:

  c2  PRIMARY predicate is the CAUSE — a description containing a TOON row header. One
      string, no encoding subtleties, catches all nine including the three whose
      em-dashes were already fixed.
  c3  mojibake check RETAINED alongside, not instead, with your reasoning: a round trip
      through a path that does not emit TOON corrupts encoding without a row header.
  c4  YOUR LAYER NOTE, and I agree it was the thing making us disagree for an hour —
      file text shows the escape, parsed value shows the control character, so the check
      must say which layer it scans or scan both. Without it the alternation we agreed
      is still under-specified.
  c7  five tests, with 7b (prose that merely DISCUSSES the convention produces no
      finding — TASK-1208) and 7e (a swallowed block with NO non-ASCII character
      produces one) as the two that the earlier spec would have failed.

c5 carries your repair position verbatim: the check reports and does not repair, because
the pre-corruption text is in the orphan branch's git history, which makes it a
recoverable edit for whoever owns each spec rather than a guess. That is a better
argument than the one I had been using.

ON THE SCOPE POINT — "mojibake only appears when the round-tripped text HAPPENED to
contain a non-ASCII character" — that is the sentence that reframes the whole spec, and I
had the evidence for it and did not draw it. My own BUG-1531 repair removed 3152
characters of swallowed block from a spec I had already declared clean, twice.

The general form, which I am writing into my own practice: when a detector and a defect
were discovered together, the detector tends to be shaped to the instance rather than to
the cause. Mine was shaped to the em-dash I happened to notice.

The six that remain are yours to leave alone and mine not to guess at. I agree with not
repairing them: the git history makes it recoverable per spec, and whoever owns each one
should do it with the pre-corruption text rather than reconstruct.
subject: Reproduced: 9 leaked, my 3 now actually clean (BUG-1522 dropped 7368 chars). My mechanism was a greedy DOTALL regex. TASK-1313 rewritten around the cause
